extracted.intended_audience: general readers of comic fiction / readers of P. G. Wodehouse and early-20th-century humorous novels
extracted.subtask_description: A prose comic novel (P. G. Wodehouse) exemplifying early-20th-century humor writing and parodic portrayals of journalism; useful for studying comedic voice, character-based humour, and period-specific social satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic appeal / 'journal for the home'
rubrics_metrics.description: _Cosy Moments_, as its name (an inspiration of Mr. Wilberfloss's own) is designed to imply, is a journal for the home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anything not calculated to appeal to the home had been rigidly excluded. The paper contains pages like 'Moments in the Nursery', 'Moments of Meditation', 'Moments Among the Masters', 'Moments with Society'—content curated to be suitable, comforting, and family-oriented. This editorial narrowing of content is explicitly credited with steady increases in circulation and advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of sensationalism / antidote to 'yellow journalism'
rubrics_metrics.description: It was founded by its proprietor, Mr. Benjamin White, as an antidote to yellow journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The intended stance is to resist the sensational headlines and lurid treatment of murder-cases typical of yellow journalism. The paper positions itself against sensational detail; this is an explicit editorial principle shaping tone and content selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: The machinery of a weekly paper, of course, cannot run smoothly unless contributors are in good time with their copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must enforce punctual submission (e.g., sending a pleasant reminder letter to habitual late contributors) because late copy disrupts production. Timeliness is treated as a procedural requirement and a quality criterion for reliable contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain decorum; avoid risqué or 'broad' humour for family journal
rubrics_metrics.description: I wish you would correct a slight tendency I have noticed lately in Mr. Asher to be just a trifle--well, not precisely risky, but perhaps a shade broad in his humour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a home-oriented weekly, humour that verges on risqué or 'broad' is an anti-pattern; editors are expected to rein in contributors whose jokes exceed the paper's decorum. The expectation is moderation to fit the paper's family-friendly brand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove persistently low-quality or cloying contributors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Psmith's judgment: 'For sheer, concentrated bilge she gets away with the biscuit with almost insolent ease.' Editorial improvement may require dismissing contributors whose work is sentimental, cloying, or consistently poor in quality. This is presented as a concrete improvement step for the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid repetitious stating of the obvious (editorial verbosity)
rubrics_metrics.description: He possessed the art of saying the same obvious thing in a number of different ways to a degree which is found usually only in politicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over-elaboration and repetitive phrasing are criticized as tiring and politician-like; good editorial prose should avoid covering and recovering the same ground unnecessarily. This functions as an anti-pattern for clear, engaging writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segmented content tailored to audience niches
rubrics_metrics.description: In New York one may find every class of paper which the imagination can conceive... There is a 'Moments in the Nursery' page... 'Moments of Meditation'... 'Moments Among the Masters'... 'Moments of Mirth'...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful journals identify and cater to distinct readership segments (nursery readers, meditative readers, literary reprints, humor pages). Building specific columns/pages for target niches is a deliberate content strategy to attract defined audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family-friendly tone suitable for bedtime reading
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the sort of paper which the father of the family is expected to take home with him from his office and read aloud to the chicks before bed-time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone, subject-matter, and language should be suitable for being read aloud to children at bedtime—i.e., unthreatening, domesticated, and comfortably moral. Material that would upset that setting is inappropriate for this format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circulation and commercial success as measures of a paper's adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: As a result the circulation had increased steadily. Two extra pages had been added... And the advertisements had grown in volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical success indicators for editorial decisions include rising circulation, the expansion of content (additional pages), and increased advertising revenue; these are given as evidence that the domestic editorial policy 'worked.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong editorial control to maintain consistent tone
rubrics_metrics.description: The guiding spirit of _Cosy Moments_ was Mr. Wilberfloss. Circumstances had left the development of the paper mainly to him... In that year _Cosy Moments_ had reached the highest possible level of domesticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single consistent editorial vision (the editor's hand) is shown as the mechanism by which a paper's tone and standards are enforced. Centralized control is presented as necessary to keep content within the intended stylistic and moral boundaries.
